stories.title: Fix api/playwright.config.ts webServer block (port + url mutually exclusive on @playwright/test 1.59+)
stories.rootCause: T17 created playwright.config.ts with both webServer.port=8787 and webServer.url='http://127.0.0.1:8787'. @playwright/test 1.59.x made these mutually exclusive ("Either 'port' or 'url' should be specified in config.webServer"). After lockfile hotfix pinned playwright to 1.59.1, the spec runner refuses to start. Confirmed in ship-phase manualQA MQA-4 (had to use local wrangler dev + curl with Host header instead of running test-ui/admin-routing-security.spec.ts).

stories.title: Remove column-level UNIQUE on pages.slug + articles.slug (global), keep per-site (site_id, slug) UNIQUE INDEX
stories.rootCause: T15 generate_about_page_stub INSERT OR IGNORE INTO pages was designed to collide on (site_id, slug) UNIQUE INDEX idx_pages_site_slug_unique. Production schema however still carries the original 0001 column-level UNIQUE on pages.slug (and articles.slug) from the single-site era, creating an additional `sqlite_autoindex_pages_1` GLOBAL UNIQUE on slug alone. This global UNIQUE makes the second site's about-page INSERT a silent no-op (IGNORE wins), even though (site_id, slug)='(S2, about)' is genuinely unique. Confirmed in ship-phase manualQA MQA-6 (2026-05-13): runner reported step_status=completed but SELECT id, slug FROM pages WHERE site_id='st_55d1985313c048d2' AND slug='about' returned 0 rows; only id=5 from prior cycle (site_id=st_a2f4f7d32e2348c2) exists globally. Same schema posture on articles.slug per `SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master`. Contradicts T1-AC6 BEHAVIORAL ('INSERT with site_id=site_b, slug=x succeeds — per-site uniqueness, not global').
acceptanceCriteria: grep -cE 'CREATE TABLE pages_new|CREATE TABLE articles_new|DROP TABLE pages|DROP TABLE articles|ALTER TABLE pages_new RENAME|ALTER TABLE articles_new RENAME' api/migrations/0007_phase3r_drop_global_slug_unique.sql >= 4

BEHAVIORAL: GIVEN local D1 with migrations 0001-0007 applied + 2 sites, WHEN INSERT INTO pages (site_id, slug, page_type, title, content_json, content_html, status) VALUES ('S1','about','about','x','{}','<p/>','published') succeeds AND second INSERT with ('S2','about',...) also succeeds (per-site uniqueness, NOT global). THEN SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pages WHERE slug='about' = 2.
BEHAVIORAL: same per-site uniqueness verification for articles table.
BEHAVIORAL: same-site duplicate INSERT (S1,'about') still fails with UNIQUE constraint via idx_pages_site_slug_unique.
FUNCTIONAL: cd api && npm test exits 0; all existing tests still pass; new test asserts pages/articles can have same slug across different sites.
FUNCTIONAL: cd api && npx tsc --noEmit exits 0.
stories.notes: Migration must follow D1-database-safety.md C-006/C-009/C-026/C-027: CREATE pages_new → INSERT INTO pages_new SELECT FROM pages → DROP TABLE pages → ALTER TABLE pages_new RENAME TO pages → recreate all indexes (including per-site UNIQUE). Same for articles. Single migration file recreates BOTH tables atomically. Existing data preserved. Must also be greppable from deploy.yml per L-008 / deploy-safety.md D1-file rule (CI deploy needs to apply this migration to production).
